subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this narrow opt-in `models.providers.*.request.rateLimit` provider-dispatch config now, or wait for the broader outbound limits design in the canonical tracker?
rationale: The PR adds public config and provider-routing behavior, while the canonical issue still marks budgets, CLI/status, tool/channel scope, and policy defaults as maintainer product decisions.

options.title: Accept Provider Dispatch Slice
options.body: Proceed after the code blocker, rebase, and upgrade-safety proof, leaving budgets, CLI/status, and non-provider calls to explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Hold For Full Design
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it in favor of a broader outbound-governance design before adding public config.

options.title: Plugin/API Boundary First
options.body: Define only the missing core API seams now and route optional rate-limit policy packages outside core until maintainers choose defaults.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider Dispatch Slice
recommendation.body: Proceed after the code blocker, rebase, and upgrade-safety proof, leaving budgets, CLI/status, and non-provider calls to explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest product-scoping signal on the canonical tracker and recent provider egress history.
